intro.title: useEffect & Side Effects
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue app that displays a live clock updating every second. You will learn how to use Vue's `watchEffect` to handle side effects, which are operations like timers, data fetching, or DOM updates that happen outside the normal component rendering flow. The main technologies involved are Vue's Composition API, `watchEffect`, and JavaScript's `setInterval` and `clearInterval` functions. By the end, you'll understand how to manage side effects in Vue components to keep your UI responsive and synchronized with external changes.
intro.usecase: In real Vue applications, side effect management is essential for features like live dashboard updates that fetch new data when filters change, form validation that triggers API calls on input, and shopping carts that sync with localStorage. Developers use these patterns when building notification systems that show alerts based on state changes, or modals that fetch content when opened. Understanding when and how to handle side effects helps create responsive interfaces that react appropriately to user interactions and data updates.
